entities.name: CASP2 (Gallus gallus)
observations: Exact full-sequence match to reviewed UniProt Q98943; 424 aa, approximately 47.96 kDa.
Caspase-2 is a cysteine endopeptidase involved in apoptotic signaling; curated annotations include apoptosis and DNA-damage-associated apoptotic processes.
Curated cellular component annotations include cytoplasm, nucleus, and mitochondrion; assignments are annotations, not direct localization measurements for an unspecified sample.
Sequence scanning identifies CARD (PF00619; residues 12–93) and Peptidase_C14 (PF00656; residues 170–415).
Reference processing annotations describe an N-terminal propeptide and large/small catalytic subunits; mature cleavage/activation state cannot be inferred from this unprocessed sequence alone.
Curated reference describes activated CASP2 as an antiparallel heterotetramer formed from two p18-p12 heterodimers.
Reference literature annotations implicate CASP2 in PIDD1/CRADD PIDDosome-mediated activation following genotoxic stress; evidence strength varies across species and annotations.
